newsitem.title: India: Police fire on Indian protesters, one dead.
newsitem.headline: Police fire on Indian protesters, one dead.

text.p: One person was killed and three others injured on Saturday when Indian police fired at demonstrators in Bombay during a general strike, law-enforcement authorities said.
Police said they had to open fire to disperse a violent crowd that tried to set fire to vehicles ignoring opposition parties' call to join the strike and stay off the streets.

The strike was called to protest at Friday's police shooting on a crowd demonstrating against the desecration of the statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, a revered leader of the lower social classes, in a Bombay suburb.
Ten people were killed and more than 30 injured in Friday's shooting in Ghatkopar 15 km (nine miles) outside India's commercial capital in the west of the country.
Police said there were further demonstrations in 35 towns across the western state of Maharashtra, of which Bombay is the capital.
State Home (interior) Minister Gopinath Munde said police also fired at protesters in Purna 200 km (125 miles) east of Bombay when they tried to set a college library on fire, but no one was injured.

Munde said protesters stopped buses and trains in 54 locations across the state and that police detained 1,836 people as a preventive measure. General strikes prevailed in Nagpur and Pune, two other large cities.

In Bombay earlier in the day, protesters threw stones at passing vehicles. Women and children joined protesters squatting at road junctions and railway tracks to stop vehicles and trains. A limited number of buses ran on relatively unaffected routes.
"There was trouble here and there. But the overall situation is normal," a police spokesman said at the time.
The atmosphere remained tense at the site of Friday's shooting and special riot police were deployed in large numbers.
Passengers were held up at Bombay's domestic and international airports, but flights were not affected.
Leaders of the Republican Party of India (RPI), which represents lower castes who deify Ambedkar, pronounced Saturday's strike a success.
Opposition leaders demanded a dismissal of the state government, ruled by the right-wing Hindu militant Shiv Sena and the nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
